intro:
BATTLE OF SESENA - 29 OCT 1936

South of Madrid, Spain

Comrade, here is your order - Move west with your armored forces and occupy the towns of Esquivias and Illescas! Support this move with your air force. Your infantry occupied Sesena and defend the town against enemy attacks. Good luck!

ORDERS
After 8 turns control 3/2/1 VH for a BV/V/TV.

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

briefing.act: ACT I — LESSONS BEFORE THE GREAT WAR

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The tank crews have painted over every marking, but the unfamiliar silhouettes of our T-26s still mark them as something Franco's men have never faced before. Spanish infantrymen watch the engines turn over and ask the interpreters whether armour can really decide the day before nightfall.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The Republican captain beside the lead company has seen the tanks only in newspapers. He has put his best infantry on their running boards because nobody told him how quickly armour can leave men behind.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: This is our first live test of a force built around tanks, aircraft, and radio. We can drive hard for the western towns, or keep the arms close enough that a local success does not leave Seseña exposed. Which lesson do we intend to learn?

choices.text: Concentrate the tanks and aircraft on a fast thrust toward Illescas.
choices.hint: Requisition an experienced eight-strength BT-5 detachment for the armoured thrust; its deployment costs 70 prestige.

choices.text: Advance by bounds, keeping infantry and artillery tied to the armoured column.
choices.hint: Attach an experienced eight-strength 76.2 mm battery and give every infantry formation 10 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Then speed is the protection. The leading companies will bypass resistance that cannot threaten the road and leave marked targets for the aircraft.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The Spanish captain is taking his men off the running boards. He asks whether the tanks intend to come back for them. I have no honest answer yet.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Give him one: the Seseña road remains open until the infantry is through. Speed may choose our direction; it does not cancel our rear.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Then no arm outruns the others. The tanks will take the towns, but every captured road must remain usable by the infantry and guns behind them.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: You have tied the tanks to marching pace on their first day. If the infantry stops at the first gun, I will remind you that this caution was chosen, not imposed.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The interpreter is waiting by the lead tank. I will give him the road order; the Spanish captain can decide whether it sounds like an answer.

orders.situation: A small Soviet-supported armoured group is committed south of Madrid while Republican infantry holds Seseña.
orders.mission: Take Esquivias and Illescas, support the advance from the air, and keep the Seseña position from becoming isolated.

intro:
BATTLE OF LAKE KHASAN - 2 AUG 1938

Lake Khasan, Far East of Soviet Union

The sneaky Japanese attacked and beaten our border troops on the Bezymyannaya and Zaozyornaya hills. Attack the Japanese with superior power and recapture the territories we deserve!

ORDERS
After 9 turns control 7/6/5 VH for a BV/V/TV.

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank (+1)
2x Infantry (+2)
1x Reconnaissance
1x Artillery (+1)

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

briefing.act: ACT I — LESSONS BEFORE THE GREAT WAR
briefing.location: Lake Khasan, Soviet Far East — 2 August 1938

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Illescas fell before the Spanish infantry expected to leave Seseña. The photographs reached Moscow first; the reports about scattered companies arrived later.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The towns south of Madrid were taken, but neither armour nor infantry can claim it acted alone. That has not stopped both camps from trying.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Spain gave us no clean demonstration—only damaged tanks, exhausted infantry, and enough success for every theorist to blame the other arm.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Illescas made speed look like an argument no staff college could answer. The tank officers have quoted your order ever since; today they expect another road to open for them.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: In Spain you kept the tanks tied to guns and infantry. Antonov still calls it a missed demonstration. The men who reached the final objective together call it something else.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: I found the photograph from Spain in the transport file. Two faces have been cut out, neatly enough that the scissors took part of Antonov's sleeve.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Put it away, Anna. This headquarters has orders, a border, and a list of names it is permitted to use.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Survey stakes disappear into the mud as quickly as the engineers plant them. From the observation post the hills look close; every approach between here and their slopes is wet, exposed, and already registered by enemy guns.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The border must be restored, but a map line does not tell us how to reach it. We can mass everything against the heights, or spend precious hours preparing lanes through the marsh and coordinating the batteries.

choices.text: Mass the striking force and keep pressure on both heights without pause.
choices.hint: Give infantry 18 experience and artillery 12 experience, and gain 50 prestige for accepting the immediate assault timetable.

choices.text: Let engineers mark firm approaches and artillery register before the infantry moves.
choices.hint: Attach an experienced eight-strength 1936 engineer detachment; the special transport and equipment cost 60 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The attack will not stop to reorganise on the lower slopes. Reserves follow the first success before the defenders can shift between the hills.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Then the casualty clerks get the true unit rolls before the first wave. I will not let missing names become another neat absence in a file.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The first wave waits for marked lanes and observed fire. We lose surprise in minutes, but not battalions in unmarked marsh.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: I will put the engineers' reports above the timetable. If a patrol finds a false lane, the battalion stops there—even if headquarters has already announced that it moved.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The photograph goes back in the transport file. The engineers' reports and the unit rolls stay on top.

orders.situation: Japanese forces hold the disputed Bezymyannaya and Zaozyornaya heights above marshy ground near Lake Khasan.
orders.mission: Retake the occupied heights while preserving enough combat power to hold them after the assault.

intro:
KHALKHIN GOL - 3 JUL 1939

Khalkhin Gol River, Mongolian People's Republic

The Japanese crossed the Khalkhin Gol river in the north, occupied the Baintsagan hills and tried to surround our troops with a two-pronged assault. Carry out a vigorous counterattack, thwart the enemy intentions and occupy the Japanese positions west and east of the river!

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
3x Infantry (+1)
1x Reconnaissance
1x Artillery
1x Fighter Aircraft (+1)

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

briefing.act: ACT I — LESSONS BEFORE THE GREAT WAR
briefing.location: Khalkhin Gol, Mongolian People's Republic — 3 July 1939

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Both Khasan heights were retaken before the Japanese staff could reinforce the saddle. The speed impressed Moscow; the roads required to hold them did not appear in the communiqué.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The border posts stand again at Khasan. So do the recovery tractors, because holding a height and reaching it remain separate problems.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Khasan ended with our flag on the heights and too many battalions below them. The official map is tidy. The transport returns are not.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: At Khasan you kept the assault moving until both heights were under pressure. The report praised resolve and buried the transport losses in an appendix. I did not.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The engineers owned the timetable at Khasan and brought the guns through the mud. On this steppe their lanes are hundreds of kilometres long, but the principle has supporters now.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Both Khasan heights were still in our hands when the front stabilised. The engineer companies that kept their roads open are available for one new assignment.

choices.text: Keep the Khasan engineers together as a field detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced eight-strength 1936 engineer detachment to the core.

choices.text: Return the companies to their formations and circulate their methods.
choices.hint: Give every infantry and artillery formation 12 experience instead of receiving another unit.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: They keep their tractors, bridging stores, and company organisation. Give them a road and they will tell us whether the map has lied about it.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: No new box appears on the strength return. The value is that every division now plans its road before it announces its arrival time.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: A windstorm lifts the steppe into the command tent. On the map the river is a blue pencil stroke; outside, fuel trucks, Mongolian cavalry, tank columns, and field kitchens are all trying to use the same tracks.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: After Khasan, Moscow asked why courage had arrived before shells and ambulances. If we go deep here, the answer had better travel in the same column as the tanks.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: A local counterattack can throw them off Baintsagan. A deeper blow can also cut the crossing and trap the force west of the river—but only if our columns keep moving after the first contact.

choices.text: Drive beyond the heights and cut the bridgehead from its crossings.
choices.hint: Give tank and reconnaissance formations 20 experience each and fully refuel the core, but do not replace losses or ammunition.

choices.text: Crush the bridgehead methodically and rebuild the river position before pursuing.
choices.hint: Restore every core formation to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition, and give artillery 15 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The heights are not the finish line. Mobile detachments will pass through as soon as the first position breaks and aim for the crossings.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Cut the crossings, but write the fuel limit beside the arrow. I will stop the exploitation myself if the tankers begin reporting hope instead of kilometres.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The river line comes first. Every captured height receives guns and supply before the next one is attacked.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: You are making success halt at the river. Give me a release condition now, or every cautious headquarters will discover one more height that must be secured first.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Fuel limits, crossing times, and the release condition go on one sheet. If Antonov loses it in the dust, he stops.

orders.situation: Japanese troops have crossed the Khalkhin Gol and seized the Baintsagan heights in an attempt to turn the Soviet-Mongolian position.
orders.mission: Break the northern bridgehead, restore the river line, and seize the positions needed to defeat the two-pronged attack.

intro:
BATTLE OF GRODNO - 20 SEP 1939

Southeast of Grodno, East Poland

Move your units across the city of Grodno to the Lithuanian border. Occupy the city and vicinity and break any resistance!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 2 enemy ground units cross the Polish-Lithuanian border (Exit Points).

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
4x Infantry (+1)
2x Reconnaissance (+1)
2x Artillery (+1)
1x Fighter Aircraft
1x Tactical Bomber (+1)

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

briefing.location: Southeast of Grodno, eastern Poland — 20 September 1939

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The Baintsagan bridgehead collapsed before its two thrusts could support one another. Moscow calls it proof of a modern operation, which guarantees that somebody will copy only the arrows.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Khalkhin Gol restored the river line and left the Japanese attack broken. It also left us a report thick enough to conceal every disagreement that produced the result.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: We held the Mongolian line, but the steppe consumed enough vehicles to make the victory look smaller from the repair park than from headquarters.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: At Baintsagan you sent the mobile force beyond the visible objective. The staff now treats deep exploitation as your signature; every ambitious lieutenant wants to imitate the part that appears on the map.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: You rebuilt the river line before pursuing at Khalkhin Gol. It was less dramatic than the arrows Antonov proposed, and it left us a force still answering orders at the end.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The printed order calls this a march to secure the frontier. The road says otherwise: Polish soldiers, local militias, refugees, and Soviet columns are all moving through the same villages under different assumptions about who has authority.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The German liaison map ends at the same northern line as ours. I folded that overlay before the refugees entered. The line is easier to share than the road beneath it.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Resistance in Grodno can be bypassed only if the border routes are sealed early. We can lead with mobile groups and risk broken communications, or keep a coherent front and accept that more enemy units may reach Lithuania.

choices.text: Send the mobile group past Grodno first and close the northern exits.
choices.hint: Give reconnaissance formations 25 experience, fully refuel the core, and gain 60 prestige for sealing the frontier roads.

choices.text: Clear the approaches in sequence and keep every formation under direct control.
choices.hint: Give infantry 20 experience and artillery 15 experience, and fully replenish ammunition without restoring fuel or strength.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The mobile group will not become an excuse for indiscriminate fire. It closes roads, reports movement, and leaves the city fight to the forces assigned to it.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: I can assign roads, exits, and halting lines. I cannot mark every armed man in a refugee column from this table. Detached groups will make those decisions without us.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Then the advance moves on confirmed orders, not rumour. We may catch fewer columns, but no detached battalion is to invent its own war.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Confirmed orders will restrain detached battalions. They will not make this march innocent. I want the arrests, shootings, and released prisoners recorded under the units that ordered them.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Record what the map cannot: civilians on the roads, prisoners taken, and every order that prevented avoidable bloodshed.

orders.situation: Soviet forces are advancing into eastern Poland after the Polish state has been struck from the west by Germany. Grodno and the routes toward Lithuania remain contested.
orders.mission: Occupy Grodno and the surrounding objectives while preventing organised enemy columns from escaping across the Lithuanian border.

intro:
RAATE ROAD - 2 JAN 1940

Raate-Suomussalmi Road, Eastern Finland

Our comrades from the 163rd division in Suomussalmi are cut off and need help. Break through the enemy encirclement and restore the supply route!

ORDERS
a. Reach the Exit Point (Road to Suomussalmi) with at least 5 of your ground units.
b. Prevent that the enemy destroy more than 4 of your units.

NOTES
a. The Finns will try to surprise you. Be aware!
b. Attention - winter conditions! If possible, equip your troops with tracked movement. Check if you can switch between wheeled and tracked movement for free.

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
4x Infantry
2x Reconnaissance
2x Artillery
2x Fighter Aircraft (+1)
1x Tactical Bomber

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Grodno and the northern roads were occupied before organised columns could escape. The speed shortened the fighting and multiplied the questions nobody wanted asked on the road.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The advance through Grodno reached the frontier. It did not make soldiers, militias, and refugees fit into the categories printed in our orders.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: We took Grodno by the narrow margin headquarters required. The border is closed; the arguments about what happened before it closed are not.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Grodno remained contested and organised columns reached Lithuania. Headquarters has sent us north before the road reports and the accusations have finished arriving.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The detached group that sealed Lithuania proved you will accept distance from headquarters. In these forests distance becomes silence after the first bend.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: At Grodno you kept the advance on confirmed orders. Here confirmation arrives slowly enough to freeze, so control will have to travel with the column.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Engines freeze faster than the mechanics can warm them. The road is a narrow white corridor through trees; abandoned lorries already mark where a column stopped long enough for the forest to close around it.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The 163rd no longer calls as a division. One battalion asks for bread, another for antitank shells, a third only repeats its map square. Every hour turns an organised formation into separate voices.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: A single heavy column carries guns and supplies but offers the enemy one long target. Smaller groups can screen the road and move through the trees, yet they risk arriving without the weight to break a roadblock.

choices.text: Keep the relief column concentrated and force the road open with weight.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least eight strength with full fuel and ammunition, and give artillery 10 experience for road-column drill.

choices.text: Split into mutually supporting groups that clear the forest before the road column advances.
choices.hint: Attach an experienced eight-strength mountain-infantry detachment and give all infantry 10 experience; winter equipment costs 40 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The guns remain together and every halt has a time limit. If the head of the column stops, the rear forms a perimeter before the enemy chooses one for us.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: One road, one target. I will report every fresh ski track, but I cannot make the forest reveal which one belongs to the detachment waiting ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Each group receives a compass bearing, a rendezvous, and authority to turn back before isolation becomes heroism. The road moves only after its flanks are reported clear.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: I will walk the first rendezvous with them. If the groups miss it, nobody at this table will call their absence freedom of movement.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Move the wireless post to the first heated dugout. A frozen operator will turn any plan back into those separate voices.

orders.situation: The 163rd Rifle Division is cut off near Suomussalmi. Forest, cold, and Finnish detachments have broken the relief route into isolated road-bound columns.
orders.mission: Open the road to Suomussalmi, get at least five ground units through, and avoid losses that turn relief into another encirclement.

intro:
VYBORG BAY - 5 MAR 1940

Karelian Isthmus, Finland

The Finns asked for a ceasefire because their front is collapsing. But before peace comes, we have to capture the west bank of Vyborg Bay and the city itself!

ORDERS
After 10 turns control 10/8/6 VH for a BV/V/TV.

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
4x Infantry
1x Anti-Tank (+1)
2x Reconnaissance
3x Artillery (+1)
2x Fighter Aircraft
1x Tactical Bomber

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The Raate road opened and the relief column came through before the forest could cut it again. The 163rd's surviving callsigns answered roll call.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Five formations reached the far end of the Raate road. The wrecks between them explain why nobody uses the word relief without qualification.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Enough of the column survived Raate to satisfy the order. The men who counted frozen vehicles instead of units use a harsher measure.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The relief road never opened and the 163rd's callsigns disappeared one by one. The surviving column has been reassigned to Vyborg with no time to pretend the forest taught us nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: You drove one concentrated column on the Raate road. The surviving guns are here because weight broke roadblocks; the empty places are here because the enemy always knew where that weight was.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The groups you sent into the Raate forests returned by different roads and with different stories. They cleared the flanks, but some reached the rendezvous after the men they were relieving had gone silent.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The core came off the Raate road without losing a formation. A mountain battalion that screened the last convoy has been placed at your disposal before the Vyborg operation.

choices.text: Keep the mountain battalion with the operational group.
choices.hint: Add an experienced eight-strength mountain-infantry detachment to the core.

choices.text: Use its veterans to refit and instruct the existing formations.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give every formation 10 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: They know what cold does before a thermometer reports it. I will keep them away from any officer who thinks skis make infantry weightless.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The battalion disappears into the replacement columns. Its habits will be harder to list and more widely useful.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: A telephone clerk writes two times on the same message: the hour the guns must open and the hour diplomats may make further firing unnecessary. Neither staff will wait for the other.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Yesterday we blamed the forest for dividing the column. Here the ice gives us every direction at once, and the clock is what can divide us.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The quickest attack may gain ground before the ceasefire. A deliberate crossing will cost less strength, but the war may end while our bridgeheads are still being organised.

choices.text: Attack across the bay approaches now and exploit every foothold immediately.
choices.hint: Gain 120 prestige for meeting the political deadline and give infantry 15 experience, but receive no replacements or resupply.

choices.text: Register the guns, secure each crossing site, and advance only behind established support.
choices.hint: Restore every core formation to full strength, fuel, and ammunition and give artillery 15 experience; preparations cost 40 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Every foothold becomes an assembly area, not a place to stop. The advance continues until the next position or the ceasefire order arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Then put the ceasefire hour in every battery order. A final kilometre is not permission for a commander to invent a final war.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: No unit crosses without fire support and a return route. If diplomacy ends the battle first, we will at least possess a force fit for the peace that follows.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The diplomats may stop the battle while our first wave still waits. I will mark that cost beside every lane the engineers save us.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The ceasefire hour goes into every battery order. If it changes, the telephone clerks wake us before the guns.

orders.mission: Secure the western shore and Vyborg objectives before the political deadline ends the operation.

intro:
BATTLE OF BIALYSTOK-MINSK - 27 JUN 1941

West of Minsk, Belarus

The treacherous Germans have launched a general attack on our homeland. The western front has collapsed and most of our troops are threatened to be encircled west of Minsk. Escape before the pocket closes! Make your way through the mess to the east!

ORDERS
Reach the Exit Points in time with at least 10 of your ground units before the enemy capture all VH!

NOTES
a. You can't deploy your air force.
b. All friendly auxiliary troops are controlled by the AI - you only command your core units.
c. Save your core units! Reach the Exit Points as soon as possible - don't get into a fight you can't win. There should also be useful attachments to make your units faster!
d. Attention - summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement.

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
4x Infantry
1x Anti-Tank
2x Reconnaissance
3x Artillery
2x Fighter Aircraft
1x Tactical Bomber

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The Vyborg objectives were secured while the ceasefire messages were still being recopied. For once the military and political clocks struck in our favour.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: We reached the western shore before the guns fell silent. Nobody agrees whether the last ground justified the last casualties.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The ceasefire found our bridgeheads barely established. The map changed in time; many units were still moving when the reason to move vanished.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: At Vyborg you chose ground before the diplomats could stop the guns. The deadline rewarded you. This morning there is no negotiator waiting to make a lost road irrelevant.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: You made every Vyborg crossing report guns and a return route before moving. That discipline preserved the force. Here the routes disappear faster than we can certify them.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The wireless net is a wall of callsigns speaking over one another. Some headquarters no longer answer. Others issue orders from positions the enemy passed yesterday. Only the roads east still provide a fact everyone can verify.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Front headquarters has sent forms for panic, desertion, and loss of command. I have left the names blank. Get the men through the corridor before someone asks me to fill them.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: We can move the core at once and preserve the one formation we still control. Or we can hold one corridor open for stragglers and accept that every hour spent helping them narrows our own escape.

choices.text: Break contact immediately and drive the core east before the roads are cut.
choices.hint: Fully refuel the core and give tank and reconnaissance formations 20 experience for break-contact drills; no losses or ammunition are replaced.

choices.text: Keep one route open long enough to gather stragglers, then withdraw as a formed column.
choices.hint: Gather an experienced seven-strength 1936 rifle detachment and restore the core to eight strength with full ammunition; the rescue effort costs 50 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: No counterattack for appearances. Rear guards disengage on schedule, bridges are crossed in order, and any vehicle that blocks the road is pushed aside.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Those voices on the road are not all stragglers. Some are crews whose tanks were issued to units already overrun. Leave them and we save machines; wait and we may recover the men who know how to use them.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The late crews will find an empty road. I will not call them cowards to make our departure easier to explain.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The corridor gets a closing hour now, before sympathy turns it into a last stand. We leave with whoever reaches it in time and we do not move that hour twice.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: I will put one closing hour on the wireless net. When it comes, Volkov moves the rear guard even if the last voice on the road is still calling.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Survival is the mission. There will be time later to decide who failed; today we save the means to fight again.

orders.situation: The German invasion has shattered the Western Front. Command links are failing and Soviet formations west of Minsk face encirclement.
orders.mission: Escape east with at least ten core ground units before the pocket closes; preserving the force matters more than holding doomed positions.

intro:
YELNYA OFFENSIVE - 2 SEP 1941

Yelnya, Southeast of Smolensk

You'll lead the attack against the semi-circular Yelnya salient which the Germans had extended 50 kilometres south-east of Smolensk, forming a staging area for an offensive towards Vyazma and eventually Moscow. Eliminate the threat and win the much-needed victory for us, Comrade!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 9 enemy ground units reach the Exit Points.

CORE (recommended)
3x Tank (+1)
4x Infantry
1x Anti-Tank
2x Reconnaissance
1x Flak (+1)
3x Artillery
2x Fighter Aircraft
2x Tactical Bomber (+1)

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The core escaped east of Minsk as an army, not a procession of fugitives. That distinction now amounts to most of the combat power in this camp.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Enough formations crossed the Minsk roads before they closed. Every headquarters stamp says withdrawal; every face in the column says defeat.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Ten formations came out of the pocket. We counted them at dawn because in darkness the column looked too small to be an army.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The Minsk roads closed before the required formations escaped. What reached Yelnya is a headquarters, fragments of units, and an order to rebuild them while already fighting.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: You ordered the core east before Minsk closed. Some call that why this command still exists. Others remember the units that reached our abandoned corridor ten minutes late.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: You held the Minsk corridor for stragglers and recovered crews we are using now. We also escaped with enemy reconnaissance close enough to read the numbers on our last lorries.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Replacement tanks arrive with factory paint still tacky. Beside them stand crews who escaped Minsk without their machines. Neither group has trained together, but the attack timetable treats them as a division.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: German traffic is already thinning behind the salient. They know the position is costly. If we strike slowly, we may capture the ground after they have removed the force that made it dangerous.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: A concentrated blow may break the salient before the defenders withdraw. Rotating the assault echelons will preserve the rebuilt force, but gives the enemy more time to empty the pocket.

choices.text: Concentrate the rebuilt armour and artillery on one rupture, then fan out behind it.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength BM-13 rocket-artillery detachment with 25 experience; priority issue and transport cost 100 prestige.

choices.text: Attack in measured echelons and replace the leading formations before exhaustion stops them.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give infantry 18 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The survivors lead the route briefing; the new crews supply the machines. Once the line opens, mobile groups move for the exits instead of fighting every strongpoint.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The new crews will believe the breakthrough proves they are veterans. Put the survivors at the head of every route conference and nowhere near the speeches afterward.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: No battalion stays forward simply because another has not arrived. Relief timings are orders, and the artillery programme moves with them.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Rotation keeps the formation neat and lets the salient empty by schedule. Give me one mobile group released the moment the first German road opens.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Put a Minsk survivor at every route table. The new crews have machines; let the men who lost theirs tell them where a road ends.

orders.situation: The German Yelnya salient threatens the approaches toward Vyazma and Moscow. Soviet command needs both the ground and proof that the enemy can be driven back.
orders.mission: Destroy the salient, take every objective, and stop withdrawing enemy formations from escaping through the rear exits.

intro:
BATTLE OF MOSCOW - 9 DEC 1941

Dmitrow, North of Moscow

The German offensives against our capital were halted and our strategic counter-offensive started. Your goal is to cross the Moscow-Leningrad railway line and to liberate the city of Klin.

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

NOTES
Attention - winter conditions! If possible, equip your troops with tracked movement. Check if you can switch between wheeled and tracked movement for free.

CORE (recommended)
3x Tank
4x Infantry
1x Anti-Tank
2x Reconnaissance
1x Flak
4x Artillery (+1)
2x Fighter Aircraft
2x Tactical Bomber

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

briefing.location: Dmitrov–Klin sector, north of Moscow — 9 December 1941

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The Yelnya salient was broken before its defenders could empty it. The first Guards designations are already being discussed; yesterday's fugitives are being offered a new name.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Yelnya proved the enemy can be driven back and that our rebuilt formations can survive doing it. Moscow needed both facts.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The salient is gone, but much of its garrison escaped. We have a victory for the newspapers and a warning for the next headquarters.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The Yelnya salient held and the proof Moscow wanted became another casualty list. We now defend the capital without the confidence that operation was meant to purchase.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: At Yelnya you drove through the rupture before the salient emptied. The new crews came out believing audacity had rebuilt the army. They have not yet learned how rare a clean opening is.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The rotation at Yelnya kept the rebuilt battalions intact. Moscow now asks those same men to pursue in winter; preservation has purchased us a force, not an exemption from risk.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Fresh ski tracks cross the map table where the paper was carried in from outside. Intelligence reports enemy exhaustion, then lists intact guns at every road junction. Both statements are true.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: At Yelnya the new crews learned that the Germans can retreat. That lesson is useful. Believing every retreat has become a rout would be fatal.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: We can pursue across the railway before the retreat becomes orderly, or secure the flanks and bring the guns forward before entering Klin. Winter will punish whichever delay we choose.

choices.text: Cross the railway in the first bound and keep contact with the withdrawing columns.
choices.hint: Fully refuel the core, give tank and reconnaissance formations 20 experience each, and gain 70 prestige for sustained pursuit.

choices.text: Clear the railway approaches and bring artillery forward before the drive on Klin.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least eight strength with full ammunition and give artillery 20 experience; fuel remains unchanged.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Forward detachments carry fuel before comforts. If the enemy stops, we attack from the march before the snow around his guns is packed hard.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The forward detachments get a fuel return every two hours. Miss one and the following guns halt, however inviting the road looks.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The railway becomes our supply line, not merely a line crossed on the map. Guns and fuel move first enough that Klin is attacked by an army, not scattered pursuers.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The Germans are already moving. If our perfect supply line reaches an empty Klin, I want that delay entered under command—not weather.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Fuel reports every two hours. If a detachment misses one, the guns stop at the railway, whatever Klin looks like.

orders.situation: The German drive on Moscow has been halted. Soviet armies are beginning a winter counteroffensive against exhausted but still dangerous formations.
orders.mission: Cross the Moscow–Leningrad railway, liberate Klin, and deny the enemy time to form another defensive line.

intro:
SECOND BATTLE OF KHARKOV - 12 MAY 1942

Volchansk, Northeast of Kharkov

We'll start an offensive to liberate Kharkov. With a dual pincer movement from the Volchansk and Barvenkovo salients, we'll surround and free the city. The main attack takes place in the south, your job is to lead the northern attack.

ORDERS
Kill 64 enemy units and prevent that the enemy destroy more than 15 of your units.

NOTES
Attention summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement, if wanted.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank (+1)
5x Infantry (+1)
2x Anti-Tank (+1)
2x Reconnaissance
1x Flak
4x Artillery
2x Fighter Aircraft
2x Tactical Bomber

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

briefing.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Klin fell before the German retreat settled behind the railway. Success has made offensive arrows respectable again at headquarters.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The Moscow counteroffensive pushed the enemy from Klin. Our columns learned that pursuit in winter can exhaust the pursuer first.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: We crossed the railway and took Klin at the limit of the force. Headquarters sees momentum; the quartermasters see what it cost to keep moving.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: You crossed the railway before the German retreat settled at Moscow. The forward detachments still trust your instinct for the unfinished moment.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: You turned the railway into a supply line before entering Klin. That patience kept the guns with us. Headquarters has now drawn a plan that assumes patience belongs only to the enemy.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The situation map shows arrows meeting west of Kharkov. The intelligence annex shows German reserves whose locations are uncertain and road capacity that is not. The arrows are drawn in thicker ink.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: I sent the reserve estimate three times. The first copy came back unsigned; the second was called pessimistic; the third is under Volkov's hand on this map.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The southern pincer is beyond our radio range, yet our orders assume its progress by the hour. We are being asked to make a local decision inside a plan whose other half we cannot see.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Command expects the northern pincer to keep advancing. We can commit fully to the timetable, or narrow the attack and preserve a reserve against the counterstroke our reconnaissance keeps reporting.

choices.text: Drive the northern pincer on schedule and force the enemy to react to us.
choices.hint: Gain 120 prestige for accepting the full offensive commitment and give infantry and tanks 12 experience each; receive no resupply.

choices.text: Narrow the first objective and keep a mobile reserve behind the salient.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give reconnaissance formations 25 experience; reserve preparations cost 40 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The timetable stands. Headquarters will not accept a smaller operation because its intelligence makes us uncomfortable.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Then leave my estimates attached to the lead group's orders. If the German reserves appear, nobody here will say the warning arrived afterward.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The reserve remains out of the opening fight even if the first reports are favourable. Its purpose is to answer the event the plan did not predict.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Holding that reserve breaks the plan we were given. I will sign the change with you, Commander; Sokolova will not carry the blame alone if the southern pincer fails.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: I will send the reserve estimate a fourth time. This copy carries both your signatures.

orders.situation: A Soviet offensive is opening from the Volchansk and Barvenkovo salients. The northern attack must support an ambitious double envelopment of Kharkov.
orders.mission: Inflict the required losses while keeping Soviet casualties below the operation's limit and preventing the northern pincer from becoming isolated.

If the mobile reserve is selected, lose no more than two core formations to preserve it as an organised group

intro:
BATTLE OF VORONEZH - 28 JUN 1942

Volovo, Northwest of Voronezh

The Germans launch an offensive towards Voronezh. Strong forces are trying to break through our defensive positions. Delay the advance of the fascists until we bring up reserves to defense the city!

ORDERS
After 10 turns control 8/7/5 VH for a BV/V/TV.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank
5x Infantry
2x Anti-Tank
2x Reconnaissance
2x Flak (+1)
4x Artillery
3x Fighter Aircraft (+1)
2x Tactical Bomber

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

briefing.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The northern pincer met every assigned target at Kharkov. The southern disaster still swallowed the operation, proving that a flawless part cannot rescue a false whole.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Our formations fought out of the Kharkov operation in order. The map arrows did not meet; the German reserves did.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Kharkov ended with the force barely extracted and the warning estimates confirmed by events. Nobody at headquarters has asked to see them again.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The Kharkov offensive collapsed before our group completed its assigned losses. The enemy reserves from my annex are now moving toward Voronezh, and the formations sent to stop them are still escaping the last map.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: At Kharkov you accepted the timetable after I placed the reserve estimates on your desk. I have brought no new warning today—only the unit numbers that survived our disbelief.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The reserve you held at Kharkov could not rescue the whole offensive, but it brought organised formations out of the salient. Some of the men digging outside are alive because you believed an uncertain report.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The mobile reserve you withheld at Kharkov survived the retreat as a formed group. Headquarters has not yet decided where to send it, which gives us one hour to decide first.

choices.text: Turn the surviving reserve scouts into a permanent reconnaissance detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced eight-strength reconnaissance-infantry detachment to the core.

choices.text: Return its crews and vehicles to reinforce the mobile core.
choices.hint: Give tanks and reconnaissance formations 18 experience and fully refuel the core.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: I will give them the unit numbers from my estimates. They have already met most of those formations once.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: No ceremonial new unit, then. The experienced drivers go where replacement tables currently show only a number.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Men from Kharkov dig beside units that have never heard a shot. The trenches are shallow because the order to hold this line arrived after the enemy columns were already moving.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The formations reported north of Kharkov did not vanish when our offensive did. Their columns are on these roads now. Intelligence has changed from a warning into the enemy's order of march.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: We can build fixed strongpoints around the objectives, or use a mobile reserve to trade ground for time and counterattack exposed spearheads. Neither method creates the reserves we are waiting for.

choices.text: Keep armour mobile and counterattack only where an enemy spearhead outruns its support.
choices.hint: Fully refuel the core and give tanks and reconnaissance formations 25 experience each for mobile counterattack drills.

choices.text: Fortify the objective belt and force every German column to deploy against it.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition and give infantry 20 experience; fuel remains unchanged.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The reserve receives fuel priority and no sector owns it. A local commander may request help; only the army commander releases it.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Release conditions go to every sector before the reserve moves. No local commander keeps it because his own trench is the one he can see.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Every strongpoint stores ammunition before the battle and marks a fallback route before it is needed. Holding does not mean being surprised in place.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Then my tanks become concrete that can still burn. Mark the fallback roads now; I will not dig crews into positions their machines cannot leave.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Mark the reserve conditions and the fallback roads in the same ink. I want neither invented after the first penetration.

orders.situation: German mobile forces are driving toward Voronezh while Soviet reserves are still assembling behind the threatened sector.
orders.mission: Delay the breakthrough for ten turns and retain enough objectives to keep the road to Voronezh contested.

intro:
TATSINSKAYA RAID - 22 DEC 1942

Bol'shinka, 200km west of Stalingrad

You'll lead a raid deep into the German rear - the target is the enemy airfield at Tatsinskaya, the primary operating base for the German airlift efforts to Stalingrad. Inflict significant losses on enemy Air Force by destroying as many planes as possible and force the Germans to divert forces attempting to relieve their forces encircled in Stalingrad!

ORDERS
Reach the Exit Point with at least 8 of your ground units.

NOTES
a. You don't have to control all VH! You just have to ensure that you keep at least one VH occupied so that the enemy can't win.
b. Attention - winter conditions! If possible, equip your troops with tracked movement. Check if you can switch between wheeled and tracked movement for free.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank
5x Infantry
2x Anti-Tank
3x Reconnaissance (+1)
2x Flak
4x Artillery
3x Fighter Aircraft
2x Tactical Bomber

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

briefing.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Voronezh remained contested for every required hour, and the German spearheads spent their strength against a defence that refused to become a rout.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The line at Voronezh bent until the reserves arrived. The ground lost is marked in pencil; the time gained is what kept the front intact.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: We bought the ten turns at Voronezh with nearly every reserve we possessed. The men now assigned to raid Tatsinskaya are the part we did not spend.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The Voronezh line broke before the reserves were ready. Headquarters is answering a failed defence with a raid deep into the enemy rear; nobody has called that contradiction by its name.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The mobile reserve at Voronezh taught the crews to strike a spearhead without being swallowed by it. They believe the same reflex can bring them home from an airfield far behind the front.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The strongpoints at Voronezh bought every required hour, but none had to move after the battle began. Tatsinskaya offers no position that can be held until relief arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Captured road signs are stacked beside the map. None points back toward friendly lines. The airfield photographs show rows of transport aircraft; the latest report shows enemy armour turning toward the same roads we need for withdrawal.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: A breakthrough joins an army behind it. A raid cuts that thread by design. Every kilometre toward the aircraft is also a kilometre the corps may have to fight twice.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: We can devote every mobile group to destroying the airlift, or assign a rear guard and open the return route before the airfield is fully wrecked. A raid succeeds only if its effect outlives its raiders.

choices.text: Drive every available group onto the airfield and destroy the transports before they can disperse.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength Il-2m3 detachment with 40 experience for the airfield strike; concentrated air support costs 120 prestige.

choices.text: Assign a mobile rear guard now and preserve a marked route back to friendly lines.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength T-70 reconnaissance detachment with 40 experience and fully refuel the core; road-security preparations cost 70 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The airfield is the centre of gravity. Demolition groups receive priority, and the column turns only after the transport rows are burning.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Write the turning hour before Antonov reaches the first transport. If the demolition teams miss it, the rear guard leaves without waiting for his pride.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The rear guard moves first, not last. It will seize road junctions on the way in and hold them open on the way out.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The road may save the corps and leave aircraft flying into Stalingrad. I want the surviving transport rows counted, not hidden inside the word successful.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The turning hour goes in Antonov's map case before the engines start. If he opens it only at the airfield, we have already lost the argument.

orders.situation: A mobile corps is ordered deep into the German rear against Tatsinskaya airfield, a major base for the Stalingrad airlift.
orders.mission: Strike the airfield and withdraw at least eight ground units through the exit before converging enemy forces cut the raiding column off.

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

briefing.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Tatsinskaya burned, the transport rows disappeared, and the raiding column returned before the trap closed. Antonov has become unbearable for reasons I cannot dispute.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The airfield was wrecked and enough of the corps came home to remain a corps. The return route cost almost as much fighting as the objective.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Eight formations escaped Tatsinskaya. Everything behind the eighth became the price of teaching the airlift that its rear was not safe.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: At Tatsinskaya you ordered the aircraft destroyed before the column turned. The crews proved what a raid can accomplish; the survivors also know exactly how late that order sent them home.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The road you guarded at Tatsinskaya saved the raiding force as an organisation. Some aircraft escaped while we secured it, and Antonov has counted every one in arguments since.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Enough of the Tatsinskaya raiders returned together to be used as more than replacements. They have earned a choice about what happens to the formation they brought home.

choices.text: Re-form the returning raiders as a Guards infantry detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced eight-strength Guards infantry detachment to the core.

choices.text: Distribute their crews among the mobile formations.
choices.hint: Give tank and reconnaissance formations 20 experience and fully refuel the core.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The title will carry expectations as well as honour. They know what it means to attack beyond help and still return under their own colours.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The raid will survive as trained crews rather than a badge. Every mobile regiment receives men who have already found a road home from an encirclement.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The staff table still carries the red arrows of last month's advance. Sokolova places blue counters across them one by one until the map tells a different story: exposed columns, tired infantry, and an enemy concentrating faster than expected.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Tatsinskaya taught the crews to live at the end of a fuel column. The winter advance taught too many headquarters to pretend there was no end at all.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: We can insist on the city approaches and risk being fixed there, or conduct an elastic defence that preserves the army while surrendering ground command expected us to hold.

choices.text: Stand on the Kharkov approaches and make the counterattack pay for every objective.
choices.hint: Gain 100 prestige for holding the approaches and give infantry and artillery 18 experience each; receive no replacements.

choices.text: Trade forward ground for organised counterattacks and keep the withdrawal routes open.
choices.hint: Restore every core formation to full strength, fuel, and ammunition and give tanks 15 experience; withdrawal transport costs 50 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The line is held by reserves behind it as much as by troops on it. Every penetration gets a planned counterattack, not a general rush forward.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The crews hear Kharkov and remember the road out last May. Give them a withdrawal hour now, before resolve becomes another order nobody can complete.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Fallback lines are issued in writing, with times and road priorities. We withdraw formations, not survivors.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The fallback lines are mine. If one formation leaves early, I answer for the gap; if headquarters forbids the movement, Orlov keeps the written order.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Kharkov has become a symbol twice over. Symbols do not protect flanks; staffs must.

intro:
BATTLE OF KURSK - 11 JUL 1943

South of Kursk, Russia

Despite our prepared defensive positions the Germans continue their advance on Kursk. You will counterattack at Prokhorovka and throw back the Germans before they break through the last lines of defense towards Kursk.

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

NOTES
Attention summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement, if wanted.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank
5x Infantry
3x Anti-Tank (+1)
3x Reconnaissance
2x Flak
4x Artillery
4x Fighter Aircraft (+1)
4x Tactical Bomber (+1)

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

briefing.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY
briefing.location: Prokhorovka sector, south of Kursk — 11 July 1943

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The Kharkov defence held every required position and withdrew before the counterstroke could close around it. The city was lost later; the army was not.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The Kharkov approaches were held long enough to blunt the counterattack. We surrendered ground with formations still answering their commanders.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: We escaped a second encirclement at Kharkov by the width of a road. The reserve at Prokhorovka contains men who know exactly what that width means.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The Kharkov defence failed and the withdrawal routes became separate battles. The formations reassembled at Kursk know prepared lines are valuable because they have just fought without them.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: You held the Kharkov approaches until the order had meaning only on the casualty list. The men do not question your resolve. They question whether headquarters knows when resolve has completed its task.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Your withdrawal from Kharkov preserved formations some called defeated. Those formations now wait in the reserve, where survival has become operational weight.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The reserve's tanks wait in assembly areas already churned into dust. Crews can hear the battle but see only runners bringing revised map references. Every hour promises better coordination and a narrower defensive margin.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: We have fought for Kharkov three times and paid each time for confusing possession with control. This reserve must restore the defence, not merely add another arrow to the map.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: An immediate armoured counterattack may strike before the enemy reorganises. Waiting for artillery and reconnaissance reduces confusion, but the last defensive positions may not survive the delay.

choices.text: Commit the armoured reserve now and seize the initiative at close range.
choices.hint: Release an eight-strength T-34/76C detachment with 60 experience and give all tanks 15 experience; emergency commitment costs 120 prestige.

choices.text: Wait for confirmed axes, artillery preparation, and marked start lines before committing.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength 122 mm M-30 battery with 60 experience and give all artillery 15 experience; preparation costs 100 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The reserve moves on the current map, not the perfect one. Leading brigades report by radio and the second echelon changes axis if the ground is already blocked.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The first radio report may be wrong. The second echelon changes axis only on two confirmations, even if Antonov can already hear the guns.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The start time stands. Reconnaissance and guns use every minute before it so the reserve enters one battle instead of twenty separate collisions.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: While the axes agree, the men in the belt spend the time for us. I accept the start hour. I do not accept calling those hours preparation without their names beside it.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Two confirmations for a changed axis, one fixed start hour, and the defensive belt's reports copied to both. Now wake the reserve.

orders.situation: German forces continue toward Kursk through prepared Soviet defences. The armoured reserve is being committed near Prokhorovka.
orders.mission: Counterattack, regain every objective, and prevent the enemy from breaking the final defensive belt.

intro:
ZHITOMIR-BERDICHEV OFFENSIVE - 27 DEC 1943

East of Zhitomir, Ukraine

You task is to defeat the opposing German 4th Panzer Army of Army Group South and the liberation of the Zhytomyr Oblast region, including the cities of Zhitomir and Berdichev.

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

NOTES
Attention - winter conditions! If possible, equip your troops with tracked movement. Check if you can switch between wheeled and tracked movement for free.

CORE (recommended - Core build phase completed)
5x Tank (+1)
6x Infantry (+1)
3x Anti-Tank
3x Reconnaissance
2x Flak
5x Artillery (+1)
4x Fighter Aircraft
4x Tactical Bomber

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The final belt at Kursk held and the counterattack recovered the objectives. For the first time in this war, the next great offensive will be ours to choose.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Kursk ended with the German attack exhausted and our reserve still capable of moving forward. The strategic direction of the war has changed under our feet.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The Kursk position survived by committing almost everything prepared behind it. We kept the initiative, but it arrived carrying a long casualty list.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: At Prokhorovka you committed on the map we had. The reserve stopped being neat the moment it moved, but it moved while there was still a defensive belt to restore.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: You waited at Prokhorovka for axes and artillery to agree. The blow arrived as one operation; every hour of coordination was paid for by the men already in the belt.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Prokhorovka remained in our hands and the core kept enough formations intact to continue west. One Guards replacement group can be retained or broken up before the winter advance.

choices.text: Retain the replacement group as a Guards infantry detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced eight-strength Guards infantry detachment to the core.

choices.text: Use the Guards cadres to train the armoured and artillery formations.
choices.hint: Give tanks and artillery 22 experience and fully replenish ammunition.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: It joins as a formation with its own officers and memory of the defensive belt. Do not spend that cohesion merely because the title looks impressive on an attack order.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Their formation number disappears, but their gunnery routines do not. The next attack will contain them in more places than one battalion could reach.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Civilian reports arrive before reconnaissance patrols: which bridges still stand, which roads are mined, which villages contain German rear guards. For the first time the map is filling with names the staff recognises as home.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: My sister's district is three columns below Zhytomyr on Sokolova's list. I have not asked her to mark the house. We issue the same road rules whether it still stands or not.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The map offers its usual clean choice: one rupture toward Berdychiv, or a broad advance that reaches more villages together. To the people under those arrows, 'later' is not a staff word.

choices.text: Concentrate on one rupture and release the mobile group toward Berdychiv as soon as it opens.
choices.hint: Fully refuel the core, give tank and reconnaissance formations 25 experience each, and gain 100 prestige for deep exploitation.

choices.text: Clear the objective belt in parallel and keep neighbouring armies connected.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give infantry and artillery 15 experience each.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The breakthrough group carries bridging stores and fuel ahead of comfort. Strongpoints outside the corridor are masked until the second echelon arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Civilian guides open the corridor. Give them receipts, escorts, and a road home; they are not another reconnaissance asset to be spent without a name.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: A broad front protects the liberated districts and gives the enemy more roads for withdrawal. I will report both results, not only the villages on tomorrow's map.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: And I will stop the first headquarters that paints a town red before its patrol reaches the square. My sister can wait one more day for an honest map.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Sokolova, leave my sister's row unmarked. Send the same receipts, escorts, and patrol reports down every road.

intro:
CRIMEAN OFFENSIVE - 7 MAY 1944

East of Sevastopol, Crimea peninsula

You're honored to liberate our beloved Sevastopol. The Germans and Romanians have already started evacuation by sea. Don't let a single man escape across the sea!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 4 enemy ground (naval) units reach the Exit Points.

NOTES
Attention summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement, if wanted.

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Zhytomyr and Berdychiv fell in a breakthrough that never allowed the Fourth Panzer Army to settle. Civilian guides reached some junctions before our reconnaissance.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The region beyond Zhytomyr is open and the enemy is withdrawing. Every liberated road now carries troops west and families returning east.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The objectives around Zhytomyr were taken, but the breakthrough narrowed before it became a pursuit. We liberated ground faster than we restored its roads.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The narrow rupture at Berdychiv carried the mobile group farther than the broad-front advocates thought support could follow. The coastal plan assumes we can repeat that reach beside the sea.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The broad advance beyond Zhytomyr left no liberated district hanging from one road. Here the evacuation clock may punish the same care.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Through binoculars the harbour is a forest of masts, smoke, and demolition fires. The road to Sevastopol is defended; the roads away from it are crowded. Every hour changes which target matters most.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Intercepts show German staffs reserving the first ships and Romanian units being told there is room for everyone. If the coast stays open, that promise will collapse long before their defence does.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: We can drive directly for the city and its political weight, or send mobile groups to the coast first and risk slowing the main assault while the evacuation routes are sealed.

choices.text: Send mobile groups past the city approaches to cut the embarkation roads first.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength reconnaissance-infantry detachment with 50 experience and fully refuel the core; coastal transport costs 60 prestige.

choices.text: Concentrate on the fortified approaches and break into Sevastopol before dividing the force.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength assault-infantry detachment with 50 experience and fully replenish ammunition; siege equipment costs 60 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The coastal groups receive the fastest vehicles and no permission to become involved in the city fight. Their objectives are roads, piers, and time.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The city will hear that mobile groups passed its outskirts while the occupation continued. Seal the coast quickly, Commander. Political explanations do not shorten a night under shellfire.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The city defence is the hinge. Break it with every gun available, then turn the released formations toward the coast before evacuation becomes escape.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Then I will keep the embarkation reports on this table while the city guns fire. Every ship that leaves is part of the price, not an intelligence footnote.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Give the harbour reports to the city staff and the city reports to the coastal groups. No one gets to say the other road was invisible.

orders.situation: German and Romanian forces are withdrawing toward Sevastopol and evacuation points on the Black Sea.
orders.mission: Liberate Sevastopol, capture every objective, and prevent more than four enemy formations from escaping by sea.
