intro:
JASSY-KISHINEV OFFENSIVE - 20 AUG 1944

North of Jassy, Eastern Romania

In our major offensive on Romania you and your troops will be deployed on the right wing of the attack front. The goal is to encircle and destroy the enemy's 6th Army.

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Sevastopol fell and the coastal exits closed before the evacuation could become an orderly withdrawal. The harbour is ours, crowded with what the enemy failed to remove.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Sevastopol is liberated and most of the withdrawing force was trapped. A few ships carried away the formations we were hours too late to reach.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The city is ours, but the Black Sea accepted more enemy columns than the order allowed us to ignore. Victory and escape shared the same harbour.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Sevastopol and the evacuation roads did not fall in time. The enemy escaped the peninsula with formations it can place in front of us again; Iași is where some of that account returns.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The coastal groups you sent around Sevastopol reached roads the defenders thought were still behind them. The staff now expects every encirclement to close with the same precision.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: You broke Sevastopol before dividing the force. The city was liberated, but ships left while the final batteries were still firing. Today headquarters wants the army, not only its cities.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Sevastopol fell before the evacuation timetable could empty its workshops. The usable vehicles and returning assault cadres can support only one programme before Iași.

choices.text: Use the recovered transport to rebuild the mobile supply columns.
choices.hint: Fully refuel and rearm the core and gain 80 prestige from recovered stores.

choices.text: Keep the returning assault cadres as a naval-infantry detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced eight-strength naval-infantry detachment to the core.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The workshops go to the columns. They will not appear in the order of battle, but the next breakthrough will know whether they arrived.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: They keep the Sevastopol name and their own officers. In Romania it will remind everyone that fortified cities can become points of departure.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The deception maps still show quiet sectors and routine traffic. The real table is almost empty: breakthrough artillery has been hidden until the last hours, and mobile formations wait beyond sight of enemy reconnaissance.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: They have given the rebuilt formation the name Sixth Army. Names survive defeats more easily than men. If the ring closes, that name will carry Stalingrad into every communiqué.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Once the line breaks, we can turn inward immediately to close the pocket, or drive west for crossings that may decide whether the encirclement remains sealed next week.

choices.text: Turn the mobile group inward and close the ring before the Sixth Army can react.
choices.hint: Fully refuel the core, give tank and reconnaissance formations 25 experience each, and gain 100 prestige for closing the pocket.

choices.text: Drive west for the river and road crossings while infantry compresses the pocket.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength 1943 engineer detachment with 50 experience and restore the core to eight strength with full supply; bridging stores cost 90 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The mobile group turns on the first confirmed rupture. No pause for a perfect front line; neighbouring spearheads become the line when they meet.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Then another army owns the western crossings. Put liaison officers on that road now; a ring closed on our map can still open at somebody else's seam.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The crossings are tomorrow's encirclement wall. We leave the pocket to the following armies and make retreat beyond it impossible.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The crossings secure next week. This week the Sixth Army is still inside the pocket. I will keep its western columns on the board until somebody reports prisoners, not intentions.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Liaison officers take both maps to the western road. Nobody closes a pocket with a pencil line alone.

orders.mission: Break through on the right wing, seize every objective, and help close the operational pocket before the enemy can withdraw west.

intro:
BELGRADE OFFENSIVE - 12 OCT 1944

West of Belgrade, Serbia

The time has come to liberate the Serbian capital from the fascist bondage! With the support of the Yugoslav Partisans and the Bulgarian Army, it should not be difficult to drive out the Germans and their collaborators.

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The ring at Iași closed before the Sixth Army understood which roads had become walls. Romania's political position changed almost as quickly as the front.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The Iași–Chișinău operation broke the front and trapped the main force. The pursuit is already crossing borders the old situation map treated as permanent.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The pocket closed, though its western seams leaked men and vehicles. The military result is decisive; the political consequences are moving faster still.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: At Iași you turned inward and helped close the ring. The result made coordination look inevitable after the fact; three armies remember how many liaison calls it actually required.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The crossings seized beyond Iași kept the pursuit moving after the pocket closed behind us. Some infantry commanders still say the mobile group left them to finish another man's battle.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Three liaison teams stand around one map and use three sets of place names. The Partisan officer knows tracks absent from every printed sheet; the Bulgarian staff knows when its artillery can move; our timetable knows only the hour.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: One command would simplify my fire plan. It would also ask men who fought here for three years to follow roads chosen by officers who arrived this week.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: We can impose one central axis and reduce confusion, or divide sectors according to local knowledge and accept that the assault will not look tidy from headquarters.

choices.text: Give each allied force a defined sector and build the timetable around local routes.
choices.hint: Give infantry and reconnaissance formations 20 experience each and gain 80 prestige from effective coalition cooperation.

choices.text: Concentrate the heavy forces on one axis under a single fire plan.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give artillery 25 experience; centralised preparations cost 40 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Partisan guides lead the routes they know, Bulgarian guns support the sector assigned to them, and our mobile group exploits between both. Liaison officers carry authority, not merely messages.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Separate sectors need one artillery boundary and one word that stops a pursuit. Agree those with the Partisan and Bulgarian officers before our first shell crosses either line.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The central axis gets every heavy gun and one traffic plan. Allied detachments secure the flanks without being pulled into a battle they were not briefed to fight.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: A single axis is easier for us and asks our allies to become flank guards in their own capital. I will carry the order. I will not call their resentment confusion.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Belgrade is a capital and a living city, not a coloured objective. Coordination must reduce both delay and destruction.

orders.situation: Soviet forces are approaching Belgrade alongside Yugoslav Partisans and Bulgarian troops while German formations attempt to retain an escape corridor.
orders.mission: Coordinate the allied assault, capture every objective, and liberate Belgrade without allowing separate commands to obstruct one another.

East of Lake Balaton, Hungary

The German offensive flagged - the enemy isn't be able to break through to the Danube. Time for us to attack. Advance to Lake Balaton and crush the enemy formations!

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

NOTES
Attention - winter conditions! If possible, equip your troops with tracked movement. Check if you can switch between wheeled and tracked movement for free.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Belgrade was liberated with the three commands meeting on schedule. Each liaison team now remembers that schedule as its own proposal.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The allied sectors joined inside Belgrade and the German corridor collapsed. Coordination survived accents, rival maps, and headquarters pride.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Belgrade is free, but gaps between the allied sectors let part of the enemy escape. Nobody disputes the victory; everyone disputes the gap.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: In Belgrade you trusted allied sectors and local roads. The city remembers who entered each district; the operations map remembers only that the lines met.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The single axis into Belgrade made the artillery controllable and the traffic intolerable. It succeeded, but our allies noticed whose timetable displaced theirs.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Recovery crews tow damaged tanks in both directions. Some are ours from the defence, some German machines abandoned in mud, and all of them block the roads the counterattack needs at dawn.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: At Seseña I counted kilometres. Today I know which recovery tractor belongs to which crew, and three of those crews are still asleep under their tanks.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Prisoners insist this was the offensive that would restore the situation in Hungary. Their fuel bowsers are empty and their recovery units are still east of the lake. Disorder is real, but it has an expiry time.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The enemy is disordered now. We can attack before our own formations refit, or spend a day restoring fuel and ammunition while accepting that more German armour will escape west.

choices.text: Launch the counterattack before the enemy can disengage from the failed offensive.
choices.hint: Release an eight-strength SU-100 detachment with 50 experience and fully refuel the core; emergency commitment costs 120 prestige.

choices.text: Clear the roads, replenish the formations, and attack as a fully supplied force.
choices.hint: Restore every core formation to full strength, fuel, and ammunition and give tanks and artillery 15 experience each; refit priority costs 60 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Leading units attack on the fuel they have. Recovery and supply follow one road behind; no formation turns back merely because its paperwork says the offensive starts tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The disorder expires at dawn. So does the fuel in some of our leading vehicles. I will mark both times and let no communiqué erase the second.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The attack begins after every mobile formation reports fuel and ammunition. We may meet a cleaner enemy line, but we will strike it with a coherent army.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: For once, the day of preparation is mine. Clear the roads, wake the crews after the bowsers arrive, and do not let Volkov turn one day into two.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The recovery tractors take the centre lane; fuel returns come at dusk and before the start. Whatever hour we choose, no communiqué moves it afterward.

orders.situation: The last major German offensive in Hungary has stalled short of the Danube, leaving armoured formations exposed east of Lake Balaton.
orders.mission: Counterattack, take every objective, and destroy the attacking force before it can withdraw into another prepared line.

intro:
ROAD TO VIENNA - 3 APR 1945

East of Vienna, Austria

The Germans are on the run - withdrawing towards Vienna. Chase the enemy and destroy as many units as possible so that the enemy cannot establish an effective line of defense in front of Vienna!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 44 enemy ground units reach the Exit Points.

NOTES
Attention summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement, if wanted.

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure! I hope for you, your next duty will be more successful. The party's patience is not endless!

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The German armour east of Balaton was caught before it could recover from its failed offensive. Interrogations describe fuel shortages more often than Soviet fire.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The Balaton counterattack cleared the objectives and forced the German armour west. Enough escaped to stiffen the roads ahead of Vienna.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: We won at Balaton after the enemy had begun disengaging. The battlefield is ours; much of the armour that matters is already on the roads west.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: You attacked at Balaton before the recovery crews cleared the roads. We caught tanks without fuel and left some of our own behind for want of the same thing.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The refit at Balaton gave us a coherent counterattack. It also gave the German rear guards the night they needed to begin this withdrawal.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The early finish at Balaton left a reserve train unused and the recovery parks ahead of schedule. We can release one new machine detachment or use the capacity to restore the whole group.

choices.text: Release the new self-propelled antiaircraft detachment for the Vienna roads.
choices.hint: Add an experienced eight-strength ZSU-37 detachment to the core.

choices.text: Use the reserve train to recover and replenish every existing formation.
choices.hint: Restore the entire core to full strength, fuel, and ammunition and give every formation 12 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The columns gain protection against air attack without waiting for towed guns to unlimber. It is a small formation, but it can remain with the spearhead.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Then the train carries replacements instead of a new unit. The strength return will look less exciting and the army behind it more complete.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Interrogation reports agree on one fact: every road west is crowded. They disagree on which columns are combat units, refugees, forced labourers, or headquarters. Air reconnaissance sees movement but not intent.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: We can drive mobile groups through the retreat and close the exits, or secure the supply roads so the pursuit arrives at Vienna with artillery and fuel enough to continue.

choices.text: Send mobile groups for the western exits and force the retreating columns to surrender or disperse.
choices.hint: Fully refuel the core, give tank and reconnaissance formations 25 experience each, and gain 120 prestige for closing the retreat routes.

choices.text: Clear the road network in sequence and keep artillery and supply inside the advance.
choices.hint: Attach an eight-strength 1943 engineer detachment with 60 experience and restore the core to nine strength with full supply; road work costs 100 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The mobile groups identify military columns before engaging and leave marked lanes for civilians. Their purpose is to prevent another defence, not turn every road into a battlefield.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Leave marked lanes before the first tank closes a road. Refugees and forced labourers do not become military traffic because our timetable cannot distinguish them.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Traffic control becomes part of the attack. Every captured junction receives engineers and guards before the leading guns move through it.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Then some German columns will escape among the traffic. I will keep their last known positions on the board, so an orderly road does not become an orderly report of victory.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Put the traffic categories on cards large enough for a turret crew to read. If we cannot tell them apart from here, we do not leave the decision to a trigger finger.

orders.situation: German forces are withdrawing toward Vienna and trying to establish another defensive belt before the Soviet pursuit can reach the city.
orders.mission: Capture every objective and prevent withdrawing ground formations from escaping into the Vienna defences.

intro:
MANCHURIAN OFFENSIVE - 9 AUG 1945

Khabarovsk, Far Eastern Russia

At the Tehran and Yalta Conference, the Soviet Union has promised to enter the Pacific Theater within three months after the end of the war in Europe. So we are going to smash the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo with a powerful operation. Your task is to overcome the border rivers near Khabarovsk and quickly advance westward into the interior!

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

CAMPAIGN WON!

Congratulations, you have successfully completed the campaign!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

CAMPAIGN WON!

Congratulations, you have successfully completed the campaign!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

CAMPAIGN WON!

Congratulations, you have successfully completed the campaign!

lose.text:
DEFEAT

You could not achieve our goals comrade, the operation was a failure!

CAMPAIGN END!

Congratulations, you have successfully completed the campaign!

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The roads east of Vienna were closed before the retreat formed another belt. Ten days later the city fell, and Europe finally stopped supplying new place names for our maps.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The pursuit reached Vienna with enough guns to finish the battle. The city fell on 13 April; the orders sending us east arrived before the rubble cooled.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Vienna fell after a hard pursuit and a harder urban battle. We reached the end of Europe with a force already being measured for another railway journey.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The pursuit failed to prevent a new defence before Vienna. Other armies finished the city battle; this group crossed the continent carrying the knowledge that Europe did not end with its victory.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Before Vienna you closed the western exits but ordered lanes left for civilians. Officers who thought restraint would slow the pursuit now cite your traffic plan as if it were theirs.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: You secured the roads toward Vienna junction by junction. The guns arrived, the city fell ten days later, and Antonov has spent those ten days calculating how much farther the first tanks might have gone.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: European place names have been erased from the board and replaced by rivers, railways, and distances most of the staff last studied before 1941. Veteran formations recognise the procedure; none recognises the country ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The tanks came from Europe by rail, followed by workshops, pontoons, and men who thought Prague was the last station of their war. Now the bridges must carry all of it across rivers absent from their old maps.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: Volkov has put the Seseña report beside the river map. The paper is yellow, the argument is not. Even Antonov has stopped pretending he remembers only the tanks.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: We can force the crossings on the first timetable and pursue before the defence understands the scale of the attack, or build secure bridgeheads that can carry the whole army into the interior.

choices.text: Force the crossings at once and send mobile columns west before resistance can organise.
choices.hint: Release a nine-strength T-34/85 detachment with 70 experience and fully refuel the core; priority rail movement costs 120 prestige.

choices.text: Secure every crossing with engineers, artillery, and supply before releasing the pursuit.
choices.hint: Attach a full-strength 1943 engineer detachment with 70 experience, fully replenish ammunition, and give artillery 15 experience; bridging trains cost 100 prestige.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The first columns carry fuel and bridging stores ahead of everything else. Once across, they do not wait for a European-style front to form around them.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: This is the wager I wanted in Spain. Now I want fuel reports, bridge classes, and a turning hour with it. Nine years have made speed more demanding, not less.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The first column crosses on schedule. Miss two reports and the following guns halt at the river, however far the tanks claim to see.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The bridgeheads are the operation's foundation. The pursuit begins when roads, guns, and ambulances can cross the same river as the tanks.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Nine years ago I would have called the bridgehead a delay. Build it. When the guns and ambulances are across, give me the road before Volkov finds another river.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: From Madrid to Khabarovsk, the recurring question has never been speed or strength alone. It has been whether command can turn either one into an operation that survives its first success.

orders.situation: Three months after victory in Europe, the Soviet Union has entered the war against Japan. Forces near Khabarovsk must cross the border rivers and break into Manchuria.
orders.mission: Overcome the river defences, seize every objective, and open the route west before distance and terrain slow the offensive.

epilogues.speaker: Anna Sokolova
epilogues.text: The river line broke before the Kwantung Army could make a front of it. When Japan capitulated, our leading columns were still moving west. You chose the wager Antonov first offered in Spain—and this time the roads, radios, bridges, and guns all kept pace with the tanks.

epilogues.speaker: Pavel Antonov
epilogues.text: The bridgeheads carried guns, fuel, and ambulances before they carried the pursuit. When Japan capitulated, every column beyond the rivers still belonged to the same operation. Volkov will say he taught you that. I will say it took him nine years to make caution move this fast.

epilogues.speaker: Sergei Volkov
epilogues.text: The leading columns crossed, ran beyond their guns, and stopped as separate detachments. Japan's capitulation ended the wider war, but not our accounting. After nine years, the first lesson returned unchanged: distance gained is not yet an operation.

epilogues.speaker: Sergei Volkov
epilogues.text: The crossings were orderly and the force remained intact, but the border defence did not break before the war ended. We preserved the instrument and failed to make it decisive. Caution can prevent a defeat; it cannot, by itself, produce a victory.
